description: Single-sample voltage spike to 412 V
lesson: A single-sample spike, not a real transient; a rolling median or z-score check should catch it without needing a physical-limits table.

description: 60 samples pinned to an implausibly low reading and flagged BAD
lesson: Flagged at the source; keep the value for audit but exclude it from any efficiency/energy calculation.

description: power inflated ~40% above voltage*current for 120 samples, quality stays GOOD
lesson: power != voltage * current is not a statistical outlier if power stays within its normal range - it is a physical consistency check the candidate has to compute deliberately, not something a range check will find.

description: 8-minute full outage of the hydrolyzer data source (3264 samples removed)
lesson: Long enough that interpolation is not defensible; the window must be excluded from derived metrics, not filled in.

description: current forced to 0 A while power stays near its normal ~29 kW
lesson: current = 0 with nonzero power is not statistically unusual for either signal alone - only the combination is physically impossible.

description: 15 rows duplicated exactly (same timestamp, signal and value)
lesson: Simple exact-duplicate detection (drop identical rows) is safe here.

description: 240 samples frozen at 30.22 while the process kept evolving, quality stays GOOD
lesson: Noise disappearing entirely is itself the signature; a rolling-variance check catches it even though every individual value looks plausible.

description: Single-sample solvent_pH spike to 27.4 (outside the physically possible 0-14 range)
lesson: Physically impossible on its own - doesn't even need a statistical test, just a hard-limits check.

description: fan_speed forced to 0 while air_flow stays at its normal ~2400 m3/h
lesson: air_flow is untouched and looks completely normal - only cross-checking it against fan_speed reveals the inconsistency.

description: 40 samples pinned to a value inconsistent with the current level, flagged BAD
lesson: Flagged at the source; keep for audit, exclude from process analysis.

description: Single-sample pressure spike to -3.1 bar (negative gauge pressure isn't possible here)
lesson: Physically impossible value; a hard-limits check catches it independent of statistics.

description: 3600 air_flow samples silently switch from m3/h to Nm3/min partway through the run, quality stays GOOD
lesson: pressure_drop is generated from the true, unchanged air flow and stays normal throughout, so cross-checking pressure_drop against the reported air_flow shows they've become inconsistent with each other after the switch.

description: pump_speed forced to 0 while solvent_flow stays at its normal level
lesson: solvent_flow alone looks unremarkable; only checking it against pump_speed reveals the inconsistency.

description: 200 samples flagged UNCERTAIN, value left unchanged
lesson: UNCERTAIN is not the same as wrong; the candidate has to decide per-calculation whether to include or exclude these rather than blanket-dropping them like BAD.

description: Single-sample electrolyte_temperature spike to -50 C
lesson: Physically implausible for an operating electrolyzer; a hard-limits or rolling-median check catches it.

description: valve_state reports CLOSED for 45s while solvent_flow keeps flowing normally
lesson: solvent_flow itself is untouched and unremarkable; the inconsistency only shows up when cross-checked against valve_state.

description: 1440 rows from this window arrive as a late batch appended at the end of the file
lesson: Ingestion must not assume the file is time-sorted; sort (or upsert by timestamp) before computing anything windowed.

description: 30 samples flagged UNCERTAIN during a suspected weather-station recalibration
lesson: Low-stakes signal; a reasonable candidate may choose to just note this rather than build special handling for it.

description: 32-minute full outage of the absorber data source (6528 samples removed)
lesson: Long enough that interpolation is not defensible; also directly hurts this experiment's data_completeness score.

description: 1350 samples frozen at 38.0 ppm, quality stays GOOD
lesson: With co2_in ~420 ppm this makes naive capture efficiency look like ~91% for this stretch - the single biggest trap in the dataset. A naive per-experiment average ranks this experiment as the best performer; a completeness/variance-aware analysis should disqualify or heavily discount it instead.

description: 10 timestamps carry two rows for the same signal with different values
lesson: Exact-duplicate dropping does not resolve this; it requires an explicit tie-break policy (last-write-wins, average, or flag-both-suspect).

description: ~20 rows locally shuffled a few positions out of chronological order
lesson: Simulates minor network/queueing jitter rather than a large delayed batch; still breaks any code that assumes strict file ordering.
